# `aitbc bridge lock`

Lock funds for a cross-chain bridge transfer.

## Usage

```bash
aitbc bridge lock [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--target-chain` | text | — | yes | Target chain ID for the transfer |
| `--sender` | text | — | yes | Sender address (source chain) |
| `--recipient` | text | — | yes | Recipient address (target chain) |
| `--amount` | integer | — | yes | Amount to bridge (in compute-units) |
| `--asset` | text | `native` | no | Asset type (default: native) |
| `--source-chain` | text | — | no | Source chain ID (defaults to the node's own chain, resolved from --rpc-url before signing) |
| `--signature` | text | — | no | Sender signature authorizing the lock (hex). Sign the dict documented under --issued-at. |
| `--issued-at` | integer | — | no | Epoch seconds the external signer stamped into the signed dict. With --signature, --issued-at and --nonce must be given together; omit both for the legacy six-field form (refused by nodes with BRIDGE_LOCK_REQUIRE_REPLAY_GUARD=true). The signed dict is {"source_chain","target_chain","sender","recipient","amount","asset","issued_at","nonce"} — canonical JSON (sort_keys, separators=(',',':')), keccak256, secp256k1. amount is integer compute-units; source_chain must equal what the server verifies: the body's source_chain when --source-chain is given, else the node's own chain ID (see GET /rpc/proposer). |
| `--nonce` | text | — | no | Replay nonce the external signer included in the signed dict (non-empty string). Give together with --issued-at. |
| `--wallet-name` | text | — | no | Wallet to sign the lock with (generates issued_at/nonce itself) |
| `--wallet-password` | text | — | no | Password if the wallet is encrypted |
| `--rpc-url` | text | `http://localhost:8202/rpc` | no | Blockchain RPC URL <!-- check-ports: ignore --> |

## Examples

```bash
aitbc bridge lock --target-chain <target_chain> --sender <sender> --recipient <recipient> --amount <amount>
RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8202/rpc
aitbc bridge lock --target-chain <target_chain> --sender <sender> --recipient <recipient> --amount <amount> --rpc-url "$RPC_URL"
```
